items.title: Sentinel Nine
items.tagline: The world's worst hero is still its only chance.
items.logline: When the legendary Sentinel Force is wiped out in a single night, the team's least-promising rookie inherits the mantle and has to learn the job in front of the world that just lost its protectors.
items.posterPrompt:
Sentinel Nine is a commercial superhero action film. After the legendary Sentinel Force is wiped out, the team's least-promising rookie has to take the cape and learn the job in front of a frightened planet.

The poster is a vertical hero shot of a young superhero character, Cassius Vale, a thirty-two year old athletic mixed-race American man with brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, glowing pale blue eyes from gene-grafting, athletic strong build with scarred knuckles, in a battle-scarred crimson-and-charcoal armored suit with a fractured metallic chest emblem of a numeral nine etched in silver, standing wide-stance on the edge of a half-destroyed skyscraper rooftop overlooking a futuristic city at dusk, glowing energy crackling along his right gauntlet, his cape torn and streaming in the wind. He is looking off to his left at a distant explosion blooming over the skyline, jaw set, eyes determined. A step behind him on the rooftop, Selene Quint, a thirty-four year old Korean-American woman with a sharp jet-black bob, dark almond eyes, in a sleek dark violet tactical suit with kinetic-shock gauntlets, standing with her arms crossed and a controlled half-smirk, also looking toward the explosion. The cityscape behind shows flying transports, holographic billboards reflecting off glass towers, smoke columns from three impact craters, a giant fallen statue of a previous Sentinel in the foreground rubble. Natural skin texture, faint sweat and ash on their faces, catchlight in each eye.

Dramatic backlight from the explosion on the right, cool blue rim from the city ambient on the left, hard chiaroscuro. Color grade: teal-and-orange blockbuster grade with neon violet accents.

items.title: Octo Heist
items.tagline: Eight arms. One vault. Zero chill.
items.logline: A wisecracking octopus and a paranoid sea turtle scheme to break into the world's most secure aquarium gift shop on the night of the annual blackout.
items.posterPrompt:
Octo Heist is a high-energy 3D CGI animated family comedy. A wisecracking octopus named Inky and a paranoid sea turtle named Slate scheme to break into the world's most secure aquarium gift shop on the night of the annual blackout.

The poster is rendered in modern 3D CGI animation in the visual tradition of DreamWorks Animation and Sony Pictures Animation, vibrant saturated colors, soft cel-shading mixed with subsurface scattering on the marine characters, expressive cartoony anatomy. Hero composition with Inky the octopus in the foreground center, a wisecracking grinning purple-and-pink octopus character with huge expressive yellow eyes, one eyebrow raised, wearing a tiny black ski mask pushed up onto his forehead, holding a stolen plush keychain shaped like a starfish in one tentacle, a glowing security keycard in another, and giving an exaggerated 'shhh' finger gesture with a third tentacle. Beside him slightly behind, Slate the sea turtle, a chubby olive-green sea turtle character with cracked spectacles slipping down his beak, wide nervous green eyes glancing sideways at the octopus with sweaty worried alarm, wearing a tiny burglar's striped scarf and carrying an oversized laser cutter that he clearly does not know how to operate. Behind them, the chaotic interior of an aquarium gift shop at night with overturned shelves, plush toys flying, a confused gift-shop manatee security guard cartoon character peeking around a corner, neon blue laser security beams crisscrossing the shop, fishbowl-shaped novelty lamps casting cute pink-and-cyan light.

items.title: The Berlin Letter
items.tagline: Two cities. One letter. Forty years of silence.
items.logline: In November 1989, as the wall begins to fall, a quiet East Berlin librarian carries a forty-year-old undelivered letter across the city to a sister who may no longer remember her name.
items.posterPrompt:
The Berlin Letter is a quiet prestige Cold War-era drama. As the wall begins to fall in November 1989, an East Berlin librarian carries a forty-year-old undelivered letter across the city to a sister who may no longer remember her name.

The poster shows Ursula Hartmann, a sixty-two year old German woman, silver hair pinned back into a neat low chignon, sharp angular features, pale grey-blue eyes turned slightly downward at the letter in her hands, wearing a heavy charcoal wool overcoat with a small silver brooch at her collar, standing alone on a snow-dusted Berlin street near a long stretch of the wall, the crumbling concrete and faded graffiti visible behind her. Slightly to her right and a step further back, almost in soft focus, Wolfram Klein, a sixty-eight year old German man, weathered kind face, deep-set brown eyes watching her from across the road, in a worn black coat with a folded West Berlin newspaper under one arm. Neither looks at the camera. Both are framed by the historical moment around them, a small crowd of West Germans pulling chunks of the wall down further along the street, candles in the snow, sparks from someone's chisel, soft falling snow drifting between them. Natural skin texture with visible pores, fine cold-flush on their cheeks, breath misting, catchlight in each eye.

Diffuse overcast key, gold tungsten warmth from street lamps, cool blue from the snow. Color grade: cold slate blue and faded ochre with single warm gold accent from the lamps.

items.title: Sound of Honey
items.tagline: Every song she wrote was for someone else. Every life she lived was her own.
items.logline: The true-inspired rise of a Black Memphis songwriter who wrote the soul standards everyone sang and almost no one heard her sing.
items.posterPrompt:
Sound of Honey is a music biopic about a 1970s Memphis soul songwriter who wrote the standards everyone sang and almost no one heard her sing.

The poster shows Halle Marquis, a twenty-nine year old Black American woman with thick natural shoulder-length curls held back with a gold hair pick, warm cinnamon-brown eyes lit with quiet defiance, full lips slightly parted as if mid-note, in a glittering rust-orange floor-length 1970s stage gown with a deep V neckline and oversized chiffon sleeves, gold hoop earrings catching the spot light, standing at a chrome studio microphone in the foreground center, one hand resting on the mic stand, head tilted slightly to her right as she looks toward something off-frame. Behind her in the dim recording studio, slightly out of focus, Vance Brutal, a fifty-two year old Black American man, salt-and-pepper short afro, a neat grey-streaked beard, deep-set brown eyes watching her with quiet pride from behind the soundboard glass, wearing a deep brown leather jacket over a cream turtleneck, a half-smoked cigarillo in his hand. The studio walls are lined with vintage Stax-era acoustic panels and reel-to-reel tape machines spinning slowly. Natural skin texture with visible pores, soft sweat sheen under hot stage lights, catchlight in each eye.

Single warm tungsten key spotlight from above-front pooling on her face and gown, deep amber rim light, cool blue control-room glow behind. Color grade: rich amber, gold, and warm sienna with a single cool blue accent.

items.title: Death in Three Acts
items.tagline: She wrote the play. They will perform the murder.
items.logline: When a celebrated London theater impresario is killed at her own opening night gala, a sharp-tongued theater critic and a young understudy investigate the dozen suspects on the cast list.
items.posterPrompt:
Death in Three Acts is a stylish London-set whodunit murder mystery in the tradition of Knives Out and Glass Onion. A celebrated theater impresario is killed at her own opening night gala. A sharp-tongued theater critic and a young understudy investigate the dozen suspects on the cast list.

The poster shows two leads center-frame in a grand red-velvet theater proscenium. On the left, Sir Edmund Cavalier, a sixty-eight year old British man with neatly slicked silver-white hair, sharp aristocratic features, knowing pale blue eyes with one eyebrow arched in amused suspicion, wearing a crisp midnight-blue velvet smoking jacket with a tartan bow tie and a small monocle hanging on a gold chain, holding a leather-bound playbill open in one hand. Beside him at his shoulder, Beatrix Wren, a twenty-eight year old British woman with bright copper-red hair in a 1940s-style victory roll, witty green eyes glancing sideways at him, full plum-painted lips quirked in a smirk, wearing a sleek emerald-green satin evening gown with a thin black velvet ribbon at the neck, holding up an evidence bag containing a single bloody pearl earring. Neither looks at the camera. Behind them, the stage of an old London theater frozen mid-scene, eight other suspect characters arranged in tableau across the proscenium like figures on a chess board, each in distinct period costume, all holding the same neutral expression. A fallen golden Best Director award rolls slowly on the stage in the foreground. Natural skin texture with visible pores, catchlight in each eye.

Warm tungsten footlight key from below, cool overhead spot from the rigging, dramatic red velvet bounce light. Color grade: oxblood red, deep emerald, and burnished gold.
